title: セールスにはいつ行くんですか  (When Do We Go Selling?)

segments.t: On their first morning teamed up together, Ono takes Muranishi straight to a movie theater instead of visiting customers. When Muranishi anxiously asks about work, Ono hands him a novel about a seagull and talks about freedom. Listen to their whispered conversation in the dark cinema.
小野さん。
正気か？お前。
今から一番面白いパートだぞ。
見せ場だよ、見せ場！
確かにそうみたいですけど。
セールスにはいつ行くんですか？
気が向いたらに決まってるだろ。
君は真の自分に立ち返る自由を得たのだ。
助言ですか？ありがとうございます。
ジョナサンの一節だよ。
空でやれることは何か知りたいだけなんだ。
ただそれだけのことさ。
Even inside a dark theater, Muranishi worries about schedules while Ono quotes literature. Let's look closer at each line.
今から一番面白いパートだぞ。
'The most exciting part is starting right now.' "Ima kara" means starting right now. "Ichiban", literally number one, sits before "omoshiroi", interesting or fun, to say 'the most exciting'.
見せ場だよ、見せ場！
'It is the best scene, the highlight!' "Miseba" joins "miseru", to show, with "ba", place—literally the 'showing-place', meaning the big highlight of a movie or play.
確かにそうみたいですけど。
'Well, it certainly looks that way, though.' "Tashika ni" means certainly or indeed. Trailing off on "kedo", though, is a classic Japanese way to agree politely before raising a concern.
セールスにはいつ行くんですか？
'When are we going out to do sales?' Unlike English, which puts 'when' at the front, Japanese leaves "itsu", when, right before "iku", to go.
気が向いたらに決まってるだろ。
'Whenever I feel like it, obviously.' "Ki ga muitara" literally says 'if my spirit turns that way'—a natural idiom for 'when I am in the mood'. "Kimatteru" adds 'that is settled' or 'obviously'.
君は真の自分に立ち返る自由を得たのだ。
'You have gained the freedom to return to your true self.' Ono switches to bookish "kimi" for 'you' and dramatic "eta no da", 'have obtained', quoting a translation about "jiyuu", freedom.
助言ですか？
'Is that advice?' Earnest Muranishi misses the quote and asks if it is "jogen", personal counsel or advice.
ジョナサンの一節だよ。
'It is a passage from Jonathan.' "Issetsu" means one short passage or verse from a book—here the bestseller Jonathan Livingston Seagull.
空でやれることは何か知りたいだけなんだ。
'I just want to know what I can do in the sky.' Reading the page aloud, Muranishi says "sora", sky, and "shiritai dake", 'only want to know', built by swapping "ru" to "tai" on "shiru", to know.
ただそれだけのことさ。

'That is all there is to it.' "Tada" and "sore dake" both reinforce 'just that and nothing more', while breezy "sa" at the end gives the line a light, storybook tone. Now let's hear the cinema conversation from start to finish again.
小野さん。
正気か？お前。
今から一番面白いパートだぞ。
見せ場だよ、見せ場！
確かにそうみたいですけど。
セールスにはいつ行くんですか？
気が向いたらに決まってるだろ。
君は真の自分に立ち返る自由を得たのだ。
助言ですか？ありがとうございます。
ジョナサンの一節だよ。
空でやれることは何か知りたいだけなんだ。
ただそれだけのことさ。
Take away "ichiban omoshiroi" for 'the most interesting', "itsu iku" for asking when someone is going, and "shiritai" whenever you want to know something. See you out on the sales route next.
じゃあね。
